newsitem.title: MEXICO: Penoles strong Q1 hidden by strong peso.
newsitem.headline: Penoles strong Q1 hidden by strong peso.

text.p: Mining giant Industrias Penoles SA reported impressively strong first quarter earnings which were hidden by a strong peso and inflation accounting, analysts said Tuesday.
"Once again, the strong performance of a dollar-generating exporter was obscured by inflation accounting and the strong peso," Valores Finamex mining analyst Christopher Albi said.
"In dollar terms, sales rose 14.2 percent to $212.3 million, but in pesos fell 4.9 percent," Albi said of Penoles, the world's largest refined silver producer.
Penoles Q1 net rose to 281.52 million from 270.44 million in the same quarter a year earlier. Revenues dipped to 1.692 billion pesos from 1.779 billion pesos.
"Strong zinc prices and big volume increases supported revenues as other metals prices, particularly gold, plummeted," Albi added.

Average zinc prices were up 12.9 percent at 53.25 cents/lb in the quarter compared to the 47.17 cents/lb in the same period in 1996. Zinc volume sales jumped 17.3 percent to 30,713 tonnes from 26,183 tonnes over the same period.
"Silver revenues, Penoles' main metal, were counterbalanced by higher sales volume in the quarter but from lower average prices," another Mexico City based mining analyst said, requesting anonimity.

Silver sales volumes hit 445,990 kg in the first three months of the year against 383,684 kg in the same period in 1996, a rise of 16.2 percent. But average prices dropped 9.4 percent to $5.02/ounce against $5.54/ounce.
But still weaker silver prices have Finamex's Albi raising his eyebrows for the outcome of the second quarter.
"Since the end of the first quarter, we might add, silver prices have fallen another 6.7 percent, a troubling harbinger for the second quarter," he added.

Analysts said Penoles did manage to bring about a substantial improvement in operating margin, improving in the quarter to 21.01 percent. Albi said Penoles outgunned fellow miners Grupo Mexico and Autlan in this respect.
"Because of its more diversfied product mix, its margin has been the most stable in the sector. In Q1 1996, operating income was 26.8 percent of sales," Albi said.
